podcast.body: An original copy of Joy Division's debut EP, released in June 1978. It featured four tracks on the band's own label, with a pressing of 1,000 copies. At the time of recording, the band was still known by their original name, Warsaw, but adopted Joy Division by the time the record was released. A copy in pristine condition can command a price of up to $12,000. "It's an original copy of the debut EP from Joy Division released in June 1978."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This four-track, seven-inch EP was the band's first release as Joy Division, featuring a controversial cover image of a Hitler Youth kid banging on a drum. It included the song "Warsaw." "From the four track seven-inch EP entitled An Ideal for Living, this is Joy Division with a song called Warsaw."
